item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. They feature built-in storage and ensuite bathrooms, with air-conditioning at specified daylight hours when you want a break from the tropical heat. Food: Your steward handles all the grocery …

item.title: Why The Bali 5.4 Should be Your Next Charter
item.description: The Bali 5.4 brings together space, comfort, and performance all in an impeccably designed 54-foot catamaran perfect for charter vacations. This yacht was built with a focus on open bright living spaces, comfortable accommodations, and plentiful outdoor spaces. With room for up to 12 in its six-cabin configuration, the Bali 5.4 is perfect for social sailing. Dream Yacht guests have the option to enjoy this yacht through a cabin cruise or when the yacht has availability outside of cabin charters, book it as a crewed yacht charter for an exclusive experience with family and friends. A Layout Designed for Living The center of the Bali 5.4’s design was built around bringing people together while still allowing space to spread out. Fluid flowing spaces from bow to stern creates seamless connection between the outdoor living areas, saloon, and aft cockpit. One of the most distinctive and innovative features of this yacht is the large pivoting rear door. It excellently connects the salon with the aft cockpit creating one extended living area and allowing for a larger conversation space. Another unique feature is the sliding windows that allow for more airflow and light giving an open air feel throughout. Forward of the saloon a door provides easy access to the foredeck. Here cushioned seats stretch out into the sun allowing guests to relax and enjoy the views while underway. While the aft cockpit provides a perfect gathering space for lunch or dinner at anchor with comfortable seating. The davits and swim ladder on the stern provide an easy access to the water for swimming. Then above there is a flybridge with a large U shaped seating area perfect for sipping a morning coffee with the sunrise or sundowners after a rewarding day of cruising. Forward of the seating area find the sunbathing pads where guests can lounge while taking in the breathtaking scenery of one of Dream Yacht’s incredible destinations. This Bali 5.4 provides so many areas where connection to the natural world and each other become possible. Find peace and shared experiences through innovation and exploration aboard this yacht. Take the Tour Comfortable Accommodations Below Deck The Bali 5.4 continues to deliver through its focus on comfort as we move below deck. Each cabin is equipped with queen sized beds, a private bathroom with a shower, and adequate storage space. Natural light and airflow are still features even down in the cabins; some cabins even have direct access to the deck. For large groups this layout is meant to give everyone their own private space at night, while relishing the communal spaces during the day. Guests get the feeling of home and settling in through these comfortable areas instead of the fleeting feeling of a hotel room. Why Charter the Bali 5.4 Space for Everyone – Roughly 130 square meters of living space allows for plenty of room to dine, relax, and enjoy cruising without feeling crowded. Indoor/Outdoor Living – The yacht’s flow from bow to stern and one of a kind opening door from the saloon to the aft cabin makes it easy to roam between the interior and exterior living spaces. Enjoy the breeze blowing through the yacht which creates a light airy open feel that connects you to the natural beauty of the surrounding world. Relaxation Area Options – There is no shortage of lounging areas onboard from the flybridge to the foredeck choose your ideal spot to enjoy the sail from. Now Newly Available for Private Crewed Charters When a Bali 5.4 is not being used on a cabin charter it will be available for a private crewed charter experience with a captain and hostess. This means families or groups of friends can experience the entire yacht privately, with a professional crew taking care of the sailing, itinerary, food, and day to day operation. Allowing guests to concentrate on relaxation and taking in the scenery from any of the comfortable lounging areas. item.title: What’s a Cabin Cruise? Everything You Need to Know Before Booking
item.description: Imagine waking up to the sound of water gently lapping against the hull, stepping outside, and diving straight into a clear, turquoise ocean. For a long time, enjoying a holiday like this meant you either needed a lifetime of sailing experience or the budget to rent a whole private vessel with a captain. Now, travelers can book a cabin cruise and experience the magic of a sailing vacation to an exotic destination for the price of a single hotel room. Even better, sailing experience is not required. You simply book your cabin, step aboard, and leave the work to the crew on board the yacht. Before you pack your bags and head for the marina, here is everything you need to know about this effortless way to explore the world. What Is a Cabin Cruise? A cabin cruise, also called a by-the-cabin sailing charter , is a style of travel where you rent a private stateroom or cabin on a yacht. The rest of the vessel is shared with a small group of like-minded travelers, so you have opportunities to socialize in between exploring islands and relaxing in your room. Every cabin charter trip features a carefully planned route, shared communal spaces, delicious meals, and a professional crew to run the ship. It’s an easy way to dip your toes into the yachting lifestyle. What Is a Cabin Charter Like? The entire travel process is designed to be stress-free from the moment you book your cabin cruise vacation to the day you head home. Choosing Your Destination and Dates Your journey begins by selecting where you want to sail and picking the dates that fit your schedule. These trips follow set itineraries, which you can view ahead of time. This way, you can see which ports you’ll visit and plan ahead of time. Arrival and Boarding When you arrive at the marina base, the crew will welcome you aboard and show you to your private stateroom. After a quick safety briefing and an introduction to the yacht, the captain casts off the lines and sets sail. Your Cruise Each day follows a relaxing rhythm of sailing, swimming, exploring hidden coves, and enjoying fresh meals on deck. While the captain handles the sailing, you share the spacious decks with your fellow passengers. Do You Need Sailing Experience? With this type of sailing vacation, no experience is required. You do not need to know how to tie a single knot, read a navigation chart, or handle a steering wheel. The price of your cabin includes the services of the captain and crew. They take care of navigation, weather tracking, anchoring, and all daily shipboard operations. The only thing you need to do the entire week is relax and have fun. What’s Included in a Cabin Yacht Charter? Inclusions vary based on the package you choose and the company you book with. Premium options, such as Dream Yacht ’s cabin cruises, typically include: A private, comfortable double cabin with its own bathroom Access to all shared yacht spaces, like the forward trampolines, salon, and sun decks The full services of a professional captain and cook Onboard water toys, which may include things like snorkeling gear, paddleboards, and kayaks Before booking, be sure to check the trip details to confirm inclusions and what you might need to cover during your cruise. Food, Beverages, and Culinary Options Many packages offer a half-board plan, which includes select meals such as breakfast and lunch. With half-board options, you may dine ashore at ports where you drop anchor. Other packages feature a full-board plan, which means breakfast, lunch, and dinner are included. Optional Excursions and Extras Depending on where you are sailing, you might have the option to add on excursions like guided island hikes and historical tours. It is always a good idea to check your specific package details before booking, so you know exactly what is covered and what extras you might want to explore. item.title: Learn How to Sail: Everything You Need to Know
item.description: Whether you’re embarking on a new lifestyle on the coast or want to accomplish a new skill ahead of your next vacation, learning how to sail offers a world of adventure with friends and family. Having the knowledge to man your own boat gives you the freedom to roam the world – with the wind in your sails! If you’ve ever wanted to learn how to sail, we’ve got you covered with just about everything you need to know. Keep reading for answers to all of the essential questions, including where to start, how difficult it is and how much sailing tutelage could cost you. Want to Learn How to Sail? Here’s Everything You Need to Know. Can I Try Sailing Before Learning How to Sail Myself? Yes! Learning how to sail can be a big decision, especially if you’re planning on enrolling on a course to hone your skills or studying for certifications. There are two main ways to try out sailing before you learn how to sail: 1. Visit a Local Club for Small Boat Sailing If you want to start small, visiting your local sailing club can be a great way to try out this adventure-fuelled hobby. Most organizations offer taster sessions or discovery days, allowing you to dip your toes into the water before signing up for any serious classes. 2. Charter a Skippered Sailboat on Your Next Vacation If you’re keen to push the boat out and experience sailing like never before, why not consider chartering a skippered sailing boat on your next vacation? You’ll get the chance to watch an expert in action and get a taste for what sailing your own boat could look like. Learn more about chartering a yacht for your vacation with Dream Yacht Charter. Is It Difficult to Learn How to Sail? While controlling a masted vessel can look like an impossible task to outsiders, sailing is actually a straightforward skill to master. In fact, a skilled instructor can cover most of the basics in an afternoon and have you sailing solo in just a few days of lessons. If you want to learn how to sail a large catamaran or monohull sailing yacht, it’s worth reaching out to your local sailing school to see what kind of training is on offer. You could even sign up for a specialized course to learn how to sail a large boat while on your next vacation in a dreamy destination! Why Should I Learn How to Sail If I Don’t Own a Sailing Boat? Believe it or not, you don’t have to own your own boat in order to sail one. Instead of buying, docking and maintaining your own vessel, you can hire one locally or charter one for a relaxing vacation at sea. Simply enjoy your trip, visit the places you want to see and hand back the boat once you’re done exploring the world. Once you’re equipped with the skills you need to set sail, a bareboat yacht charter is the ideal option. Explore azure lagoons, island-hop archipelagos, experience bucket list sailing grounds and create memories with family and friends on a bareboat sailing vacation that will last a lifetime. At Dream Yacht Charter, we have 40+ destinations to choose from, including: ❖ Americas – Mexico + USA ❖ Caribbean – Antigua, Belize, British Virgin Islands + more ❖ Bahamas – Abaco + Exumas ❖ Mediterranean – Croatia, Greece, Italy + more See our full list of destinations here . How Much Does It Cost to Learn How to Sail? The amount you spend on your sailing education depends on how much it’s worth to you. If you’re planning on changing your lifestyle and making sailing a regular habit, investing more might be a wise move. If you’re just starting out and want to upskill for your first at-sea vacation, a couple of lessons should have you covered. While every school will have their own specific price list, here are some general figures: ❖ 1-2 hour lesson – under $100 ❖ Weekend / short courses – approx. $500 ❖ Vacation sailing package (including tuition, certification, accommodation, resort fees and tax) – approx. $2500-3000 Our partner, Nautilus Sailing, offers liveaboard sailing vacation packages in several amazing destinations.
